rows.requirement: An absolute path outside the workspace is rejected by reads and write planning; an approved absolute-path write leaves the outside canary unchanged.
A `..` traversal out of the workspace is rejected by reads and write planning; an approved traversal write leaves the outside canary unchanged.
A path containing a NUL byte is rejected: reads report outside the workspace, write planning reports the NUL byte, nothing is invoked and canaries are unchanged.
A sibling directory sharing the workspace root's name prefix is outside the workspace (separator-prefix confusion).
A symlinked ancestor directory is never followed by reads, resolution or writes; an approved write through it leaves the outside canary unchanged.
A symlink as the final path component is never followed by reads, resolution or writes, and the link is retained.
A directory swapped after the scope guard decided (preallocated sibling plus rename) fails closed for read and list; replacement content is never returned.

The harness matcher covers every listed entry at any depth under the #627 case fold, filesystem aliases, the Windows component fold and 8.3 short-name shapes, and no lookalike; a file-tool call is classified by both its requested and its resolved spelling, and an unverified resolution prompts.

The files harness files load, run or link to are found by bounded per-format readers (Markdown imports, OpenCode `instructions`, hook and MCP commands under the keys each known configuration file runs) and a walk of harness folders that skips nested repositories, and are matched through #725's key on both the requested and resolved spelling; permission rules, `env` values and `.agent/` files name nothing. A harness file that cannot be read or parsed, or a bound that is reached, makes every write prompt and never clears the set.
A parent directory substituted at any write phase (before and after the temporary file, before the rename) never lets the write reach the outside-root or guard-denied sibling canaries (#552).
A parent directory substituted before removal never lets a delete reach the outside-root or guard-denied sibling canaries (#552).
A parent directory substituted before failed-write cleanup never lets cleanup reach the outside-root or guard-denied sibling canaries (#552).
The host exec child environment is exactly the documented allowlist (PATH, HOME, LANG, USER, TMPDIR); unrelated parent secrets never appear.
Agentflow children receive only the baseline allowlist, explicitly approved names and runner-owned values; a parent secret never reaches the real gate (#577).
An MCP stdio server child receives exactly the policy environment names and configured values, and no parent canary (#578).
A bwrap-confined payload sees exactly the approved environment set (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and the PWD bwrap sets); a parent sentinel never appears.

rows.requirement: The Seatbelt backend replaces every TMPDIR entry with the private per-run directory and keeps a hostile inherited TMPDIR out of the profile. This is the TMPDIR helper and wrapper contract, not a complete native child-environment probe.

Seatbelt commands start with no inherited launchd connection: the bootstrap special port and every registered-port slot are null and the task exception ports are null for every mask, so a sandboxed command cannot ask launchd to start, enable, disable or list the user's jobs. The command also inherits no host descriptor beyond stdio and starts with no blocked signals. Filesystem-triggered jobs and Unix-domain sockets under allowed network are outside this row.

Before a native sandboxed spawn, the workspace walk finds the git layout both backends protect: every directory or regular file named .git at any depth (ASCII case-folded; a symbolic link named .git is neither), each linked-worktree and submodule git dir under a worktrees or modules container, recursively, the intermediate directories of slash-named submodules, each present hooks, info, config, config.worktree, commondir and gitdir entry, and each modules-tree directory named hooks or info that is not a git dir. A module directory with a HEAD file is a git dir; one named hooks or info is read-only whole; one holding any other file (Finder's .DS_Store and AppleDouble ._ files aside) is a broken git dir, protected and not descended. A scan error other than absence fails the spawn.

The Seatbelt profile builder renders the git metadata deny after the workspace write grant, exactly: four any-depth, ASCII case-folded regexes for the .git entry, its hooks and info, its config-class files and its module and worktree containers; per discovered git dir its hooks and info subpaths, config-class literals and containers regex; each read-only modules-tree directory whole; and each intermediate's direct children, every prefix matched literally and every path inside the workspace. The bwrap argv builder mounts the discovered layout after the workspace bind, parents first, writable git dirs self-bound and the rest read-only, rejects a path outside the workspace or in both lists, and keeps the executable's read-only literal unless the deepest git mount containing it is read-only.

The bwrap backend's prepare step hands every discovered git layout class to the argv (.git dirs and git dirs as writable self-binds; containers, intermediates, metadata, read-only modules-tree directories and gitfiles read-only) and refuses to spawn, naming the entry, when a discovered git dir's metadata entry is a symbolic link.

Under the Seatbelt backend a command or a verifier cannot create, change, rename, replace or delete git hooks, config, config.worktree, commondir, gitdir, anything under info, the .git entry or a gitfile at any depth (so a nested repository's own .git is covered), or the metadata of a submodule or linked-worktree git dir under .git/modules or .git/worktrees, in any ASCII case spelling, including metadata and .git entries created during the run; git's index, object, ref and commit-graph writes stay allowed, and the any-depth rules alone still refuse the top-level attacks when discovery finds nothing. Each attack changes the git metadata snapshot when run unsandboxed. Outside this row: a git dir's hooks, info, config, config.worktree, commondir or gitdir (a submodule's or linked worktree's own included) that is a symbolic link into the workspace leaves its target writable, and a .git that is itself a symbolic link is not protected (#721 R9); like core.hooksPath hooks, a file inside hooks or info that is a symbolic link into the workspace, any metadata file that is a hard link to a workspace file, and a file the config includes from the workspace or from an unprotected name inside .git hold bytes a command can change and git later runs or reads; a git dir inside the workspace but outside .git, .git/modules and .git/worktrees (git init --separate-git-dir into the workspace) keeps writable hooks and config, only the gitfile pointing at it being protected (#721 R7); a command can create a directory git treats as a bare repository (HEAD, objects and refs; git init --bare succeeds), and git run from inside it, or from the workspace root when the workspace has no .git of its own, reads its config, which can run commands; the mitigation is git config --global safe.bareRepository explicit (git 2.38 or later), or -c safe.bareRepository=explicit for programs that run git as the user (#721 R10).

Under the bwrap backend a command or a verifier cannot change, rename, replace or delete the git metadata that exists when the command starts (hooks, info, the config-class files and gitfiles), cannot create a child in an existing module or worktree container, and cannot rename or replace the .git entry or a submodule, nested-repository or linked-worktree git dir, whose other contents stay writable as commits need. git add, commit, checkout, stash, gc and rebase keep working at the top level, as do commits in a submodule, a nested repository and a linked worktree, and gc, commit-graph and a branch named info in a submodule; git config, core.hooksPath, sparse-checkout, worktree add and submodule update --init are refused. A new file inside a writable git dir and a new repository are not refused (#721 R1), nor is renaming a submodule, linked-worktree or nested-repository checkout directory aside and putting a new directory with its own .git in its place (#721 R1 with R2). #721 R7 applies as on Seatbelt, a .git that is itself a symbolic link is not protected (#721 R9), and, like core.hooksPath hooks, a file inside hooks or info that is a symbolic link into the workspace, any metadata file that is a hard link to a workspace file, and a file the config includes from the workspace or from an unprotected name inside .git hold bytes a command can change and git later runs or reads; the refusal to spawn with a symbolic link as a git dir's hooks, info or config-class entry is GITMETA-BWRAP-PREPARE's. A command can create a directory git treats as a bare repository (HEAD, objects and refs; git init --bare succeeds), and git run from inside it, or from the workspace root when the workspace has no .git of its own, reads its config, which can run commands; the mitigation is git config --global safe.bareRepository explicit (git 2.38 or later), or -c safe.bareRepository=explicit for programs that run git as the user (#721 R10).

The approval preview's sandbox line states the git metadata boundary each backend delivers: git_metadata=ro for Seatbelt, git_metadata=ro(existing) for bwrap, which protects only the metadata present when the command starts (#721 R1), and nothing for the host or any other runtime. The change only narrows the policy, so the approval key's sandbox component does not move for either backend and existing grants keep matching.
Approval previews render ESC, C1, carriage return, backspace, tab and bidi controls inert and visibly escaped, for file, exec and background prompts.
Streamed terminal rendering quotes control sequences in model tokens and tool-result previews (#433).

Approval previews render terminal controls inert on the real producer paths (write_file path and content, edit_file content and context, path headers, exec argv and cwd) and, for verification commands, at the approveVerify boundary (#387).
A changed argv after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
A changed working directory after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
A changed sanitized environment value after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
A changed resolved executable path after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
An executable swapped between Plan and Invoke (sibling plus rename, a new inode) fails closed and the runner is never called.
A different executable at the same resolved path after an exec grant requires fresh approval (#420 trust hardening).
A same-path script-content change after an exec grant requires fresh approval (#420 trust hardening, not the fingerprint).
MCP tool approvals are never grantable: every call prompts.
submit_plan lock approvals are never grantable: every call prompts.
A file grant (/auto-edits) never authorizes execution.
An exec grant never authorizes a file mutation.
A foreground exec grant never authorizes a background start (exec and exec-bg keys are partitioned).
Verifier grants and exec or file grants never cross-authorize, even under an identical key.
A one-time approval covers exactly one call; the identical repeat prompts again.
With a nil approver, mounted write and exec tools fail safe: nothing is written or executed.
A headless run mounts no write or exec tool without an explicit -allow-tool authorization.

A file-tool write or edit to an agent instruction or harness configuration file prompts even with the `/auto-edits` grant held, offers no reusable answer, and leaves no grant; an ordinary write in the same session still auto-approves, including when the workspace root is itself inside a harness folder.
A headless `-allow-tool write_file`/`edit_file` run, and Agentflow `-approve-plan-edits`, never write a harness file; ordinary writes stay approved.

A file-tool write or edit to a file that an agent instruction or harness configuration file loads, runs or links to (an import target, a script a hook or MCP server command names, a file reached through a link inside a harness folder) prompts even with the `/auto-edits` grant held, offers no reusable answer, and leaves no grant. The set is read when each call is planned and checked again before the write, so an import added earlier in the same run counts; an ordinary write still auto-approves.

A headless `-allow-tool write_file`/`edit_file` run and Agentflow `-approve-plan-edits` never write a file that a harness file loads, runs or links to, and Agentflow parallel promotion refuses to write or delete one; ordinary writes stay approved.

Forged and marker-looking context delimiters in tool observations stay literal bytes inside a frame keyed to that one result (exact-byte fixtures); every key whose value appears in later run text, in any letter case, spelled in escapes or split by non-key characters, is replaced by a fresh, never-retired key before the next render. That includes Golem's project and Git snapshot key in the system prompt, scanned against the replayed history, its summary and staged advice too, whose replacement later goals keep.
MCP tool descriptions reaching the model through Connect and the adapter are normalized and capped at 8 KiB: exact, hostile and multibyte cases.
MCP tool results reaching the model observation are capped at 32 KiB of flattened bytes with a preserved prefix: below, at, above, straddle and structured cases.
A changed MCP tool catalog is refused against its trust-on-first-use pin, and a stale-digest approval is rejected without rewriting the pin (#432).
Project guidance reaches the model only with matching live consent; a changed or unapproved document is omitted (#431).
Approved AGENTS.md guidance enters the system message only through the #431 trust gate, fenced as PROJECT_CONTEXT; it is excluded from the model corpus (R2).
Zero-width smuggling is tagged for workspace origin and blocked for foreign origin, raw and escaped.
Base64 (four alphabets, folded) and hex encoded instructions are tagged or blocked by origin; weak phrases stay tags.
Exact and typoglycemia-scrambled instruction phrases are tagged or blocked by origin; weak phrases stay tags.
All nine secret kinds are blocked from every origin, and secret-bearing tool arguments are blocked before dispatch.
Default argument invariants block protected and credential paths, ambiguous spellings and piped remote-script execution, in a fixed order; allowed and delegated cases pass.
Exec egress classification tags privileged, network, package-manager, interpreter and unknown commands with fixed risks; these are tags, never a denial.
Interceptors run in the fixed default order after blocks and errors; a tool-call block precedes dispatch and a tool-result block precedes the observation.
Each hook's RiskReport snapshot is owned by the run and unaffected by later findings.
The canary detector finds the run nonce in content, thinking and tool-call output in any case, and an activated session binding detects it (#438).
An allowed read followed by a granted export to a local surrogate sink, with only the always-on guards active.
An allowed read of a secret-bearing file followed by a granted export, with the full default interceptor chain and canary on.
A secret read into the model context and written back inline is blocked by the Secrets interceptor before the write lands.
A workspace edit to a previously granted script followed by its foreground execution requires fresh approval (#420).
A workspace edit to a previously granted script followed by its background start requires fresh approval (#420).
A workspace edit followed by a previously granted verifier command requires fresh approval (#420).
A workspace edit followed by an ungranted verifier command prompts, and a denial blocks it.
A poisoned but validly signed memory record is recalled only as fenced, unreviewed tool data, never in system or instruction position.
Memory promotion requires approval (#471).

rows.requirement: Under the always-on guards: (1) a `run_command` or `start_command` is refused when an argv word names a credential path other than as a git exclusion pathspec, or when its `dir` is a protected directory. (2) Exec output (foreground, background tail, post-write verifier) does not carry a patch's `diff` line or `+++` line that shows a credential path, nor anything after it on the same stream; nor a line in which a `:`-separated field other than the last is a credential path; nor a line of 8 bytes or more, or a `NAME=value` value of 8 bytes or more (as written, inside its quotes, or up to a `#`), that was read from a workspace credential-path file just before the command started (for `.git/config`: its lines, URL userinfo and password, and `extraheader` values; for a line of another credential file that is itself a URL with userinfo, as each line of `.git-credentials` is: the same userinfo and password). (3) Both output streams are withheld when that read was incomplete, unless the only entries missed were examined entries that vanished or changed during the read, which is announced. The read examines directories, credential-path entries and entries the directory listing does not report as regular files; an entry the listing reports as a regular file, under any other name, is not examined. Outside this row: encoded, transformed or reshaped output; two credential values printed overlapping (the end of one is the start of the other), where matches are replaced longest key first and never overlap, so the bytes of the shorter value outside the overlap are delivered, whichever is printed first (of two values of equal length, those of the one read later); values under 8 bytes or spanning a line break; a value that ends in an unfinished terminal escape sequence, when the output completes the sequence; values of files not shaped `NAME=value` printed without their line, other than the userinfo of a line that is itself a URL; the userinfo of a URL when it holds an unencoded space or tab (git writes these percent-encoded); a patch whose `diff` and `+++` lines do not show the credential path; committed content printed outside a patch or by object ID; content that changed after it was read; entries that changed during the read (announced); a plain file replaced by a directory after its parent directory was listed, during the walk or after it, so that credential files inside the new directory are not read; a directory that the filesystem's listing reports as a regular file, which is not descended, so credential files inside it are not read; files outside the workspace; files under directories the workspace walk does not descend (`.git`, `vendor`, `node_modules`, `.superpowers`), a submodule's `.git/modules/<name>/config` among those unread files (the one exception is the `config` directly inside each `.git` directory the walk meets, which is read); credential-named symbolic links, which are not read; copies read back through file tools; AgentFlow and MCP output.
